title: Potential LSASS memory dump through rundll32 and comsvcs
description: Detects rundll32 invoking the comsvcs MiniDump export or ordinal 24, a documented process-dump primitive that can target LSASS. The process event alone does not resolve the target PID.

hypothesis.summary: An adversary may invoke comsvcs through rundll32 to dump LSASS memory and obtain credentials.
hypothesis.rationale: The combination of rundll32, comsvcs and its MiniDump export is a high-signal credential-dumping pattern, although authorized incident response or diagnostic collection can use the same Windows components.
hypothesis.detection_goal: Identify rundll32 command lines that invoke comsvcs with MiniDump or ordinal 24 while leaving unrelated rundll32 activity and incomplete events unmatched; confirm the target PID during triage.

data_sources.name: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint process events

triage.summary: Resolve the target PID, confirm whether it was LSASS or another process and determine whether the dump was authorized before containment.
steps: Review the complete command line, process tree, target PID, output path, signer information and initiating account.
Confirm whether an approved diagnostic, incident-response or forensic workflow intentionally created the dump.
Inspect access to LSASS, dump-file creation and subsequent archive, credential use or outbound-transfer activity; isolate the device if unexplained.
false_positives: Authorized crash diagnostics, forensic acquisition and incident-response workflows using comsvcs MiniDump

validation.expected_outcome: Match only when rundll32 invokes comsvcs with MiniDump or ordinal 24; treat LSASS targeting as a triage question and do not match unrelated DLL execution, other processes or incomplete events.
